To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency of EGFR mutations in lung adenosquamous carcinomas (ASCs) was higher than that in lung squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) and that the frequency of K‐ras mutations was higher in SCCs than in ASCs.

the frequency of K‐ras mutations in adenosquam‐ ous carcinoma of the lung is significantly higher than in squamous cell carcinoma, and that K‐ras mutations and epidermal growth fac‐ tor receptor mutations are mutually exclusive in adenosquamoses.
EGFR mutations were detected in 11 of 15 cases (73%) of adenosquamous carcinomas, and that the frequency was higher in the squamous cell component than in the adenocarcinoma component.

mutations in the epidermal growth receptor (EGFR) gene and K‐ras gene are mutually exclusive in adenosquam‐ ous carcinoma (ASC) of the lung.

adenosquamous lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease with a wide range of genetic abnormalities.
